**Group:** Diatoms  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A deliberately lumped (super) class for three cylindrical, chain-forming centric diatoms that look very similar in Planktivore imagery: Guinardia, Dactyliosolen, and Cerataulina. Cells are elongate cylinders (drum- to rod-shaped) joined valve-to-valve into straight or gently curved chains, often with fine connecting spines or a small external process, and in Cerataulina low rounded elevations. Because the valve details that separate the three are usually not resolvable here, they are labelled together. Key features: cylindrical cells, valve-to-valve chains, no long lateral setae.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **rhizosolenia_proboscia** | Rhizosolenia/Proboscia are much longer, needle-like single cylinders with a drawn-out apical process; this group forms shorter drum-like cylinders in chains. |
| **chaetoceros** | Chaetoceros bears long thin setae from the cell corners; these cylindrical diatoms lack setae and join valve-to-valve. |
| **skeletonema** | Skeletonema chains show a clear gap bridged by a ring of marginal tubes; this group's cells abut more directly without that laddered gap. |
